title: Diego de Ibarra, Paris, 10 July 1593, in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher (BnF fr. 3984 no. 68)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's Spanish page fetched as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: his key tables are images, and two of them cover exactly the folios this entry cites.

The catalogue's piece numbers resolved to folios through the BnF depouillement, and the folio-to-canvas map for fr. 3983 and fr. 3984 built by reading folio numbers off top strips and interpolating; all four leaves located.
No. 68's figures run far higher and the leaf carries three-letter word groups, so it is the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, as Tomokiyo's citation of f. 145 says, not the cipher of the other three.

No. 68 read from deskewed strips with keyM.tsv (Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table): the clear opening and the first cipher lines (the other three letters read the same day with the office key, sessa1593).
The obvious candidate for the missing Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature, fr. 3995 f. 101, fetched and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

no. 68 line 11 transcribed and decoded with keyM.tsv as a test: syllables but no Spanish (va le ri a no la vi o xur que le de di as se ri as ...), as on lines 7-10. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table gives no continuous text on the body, and the nomenclature is missing; lines 12-31 were not transcribed. (Superseded the same day: the failure came from truncated transcriptions; see the next steps.)
no. 68 transcribed in full from a 3600-px crop: 20 cipher lines, 598 groups (ct68.txt); the earlier 28-line estimate was wrong.

keyM decode of ct68.txt scored with the es-golden-age 5-gram (no spaces): -2.500 per character against a maximum of -3.378 for 200 value-shuffled keys. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table is real on this leaf and gives Spanish (a mi no me parece que puede, todo lo que se puede, pareceria que venia a ayudar, no estamos desesperados).
Unconstrained hill-climb of all numbers (anneal68.py) collapsed onto que (score -1.59, nonsense); rejected.

Constrained fill of the numbers missing from keyM (fill68.py): 57 = li accepted (top candidate, gain far above median; peligro, aliento). 64 (ha by context) not separated from na by the LM, left unread; 31, 77, 81, 95 and the 200/800 T groups undetermined. Cribs Feria, Mansfeld, Liga fit no syllable run; Paris and Su Magestad are in clear.
no. 68 scored for sense: 224/598. The new value belongs to the Mansfeld cipher, so the doubtful groups of nos. 45/79/47 (office key) gained nothing.

Entry split from sessa1593 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 68 is in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, not the office cipher of nos. 45/79/47. Files moved; dec68.py rerun with fill68.json (598 tokens); sense rows moved to sense68.tsv: 224/598.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): ct68.txt; texts/no68_decryption.md is the saved output of dec68.py with fill68.json (all 20 cipher lines), reading68.md the earlier hand reading of ll. 4-10; key keyM.tsv + fill68.json.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/no68_decryption.md and reading68.md read: the decode is a stream of syllables with the three-letter word codes unread in most clauses; a few phrases are intelligible, no sentence can be built (docs/_check_reading.py: 0 of 3 and 14 of 30 sentences clean, the clean ones mostly the clear opening). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key work kept as a part); fraction_read 0.375 -> 0.

Re-read brief b28, step 1: neighbouring folios of fr. 3984 opened through openapi.bnf.fr IIIF (canvases 232-303 thumbnails; full images of 242-245, 262, 265, 268, 272). Found: f. 130 = Mansfeld to Feria, Formentieres 7 July 1593, wholly in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher; f. 131r-v = contemporary French decipherments of that letter and of Feria's 10 July 1593 letter (cipher f. 143). No decipherment of no. 68. DECODE has no record of this correspondence.
f. 130 cipher transcribed (texts/f130_mansfeld_ct.txt) and the f. 131 decipherments transcribed as written (texts/f131_decipherment.txt).

f. 130 decoded with keyM + 57 = li (b28_ibarra_dec.py) and aligned with its contemporary decipherment: alphabet and syllabary confirmed; values fixed: 64 ha, 63 he, 62 hi, 31 jo, 19 fa, 81 vi (h-, j-, f-rows of Tomokiyo's table), codes xen Infanteria, pun hombre, fon Flandes, dir Magestad, Vas senor, con fuerca; mon = gente and tel = exercito fit every occurrence where the clerk varied (flagged for review). The clerk left the other three-letter groups blank too.

no. 68 decoded with the new values, marks re-read on the Gallica full image where needed; partial reading texts/no68_reading_b28.md (0.258 clean sentences, 0.355 explicit holes; before 0.000). Stays decoded, not read: ~30 three-letter code groups without value (no-key-material).

Method restored: key obtained by Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld key, which cites this folio (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Feria's own letter in the same cipher (fr. 3984 f. 143, 10 July 1593, 150 groups) transcribed in two passes and aligned with its contemporary decipherment f. 131v (texts/f143_feria_ct.txt, texts/f143_alignment.md): 89 = yu, 77 + loop = pli, len = grand-, mark ^ = -n, 64 = ha confirmed; by context ner = necesidad (2x) and gur = -mente (encarecidamente; no. 68 l. 20 abundantemente). no. 68 about 0.266 clean (from 0.258); still decoded, not read. No fresh portion exists for a measurement.

PR #548 checked: f. 143 transcription compared with the Gallica image (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF, canvas 265, 2400 px), all eight cipher lines: the groups agree, the doubtful places are those flagged (P1 '23 5?' may be '2 35'; 76 and ter* carry marks of uncertain form); own decoder (keyM.tsv + b28 values + 89 yu, 77 pi; marks ª -n, ° -s, . -r) reproduces the alignment, 22 of 150 groups are codes or unread. 89 = yu and 77 = pi fill the gaps of Tomokiyo's y- and p-rows; the mark ª = -n is Tomokiyo's 'v final -n' mark, confirmed, not new. ner and gur rest on context only (holes by the read bar); no. 68 class and fraction unchanged (not read, 0).

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld key, which cites this folio, applied (read with known key, recorded under parts), decodes the syllabic figures, but the three-letter word codes that carry much of the sense have no table, and the letter does not build sentences. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld key, which cites this folio; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document does not build sentences, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.375, sense68.tsv (224 of 598 groups of ct68.txt marked as forming Spanish sense), which counted phrases scattered among unread codes.
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from sessa1593. The syllables read; the three-letter word codes, which carry much of the sense, have no published table.

gaps.detail: the three-letter nomenclature (pra, dur, hes, gar, rom, vul, cil, var, vis, tor, xur ...) is published nowhere and no crib fixes it (f. 130 and f. 143 with their 1593 decipherment fix xen, pun, mon, tel, fon, dir, Vas, len; ner and gur are placed by context only and count as holes); 77 = pi from f. 143, but its two occurrences in no. 68 give no sense; 95, 200T, 800T unplaced; diacritic finals dropped in ct68.txt

texts.note: Decoded, not read: re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b28). The sibling letter in the same key, Mansfeld to Feria 7 July 1593 (fr. 3984 f. 130), and its contemporary French decipherment (f. 131r-v) fix 64 = ha, 63 = he, 62 = hi, 31 = jo, 19 = fa, 81 = vi and the codes xen = Infanteria, mon = gente, pun = hombre, tel = exercito, fon = Flandes (texts/codes_b28.json); with them a third of no. 68's sentences build (partial reading texts/no68_reading_b28.md, 0.258 clean, 0.355 explicit holes). The rest break on ~30 three-letter code groups (pra x6, xur x3, gar, dur, var, tor, vis ...) that no table gives and that the 1593 decipherer also left blank. Blocker: no-key-material. 13 Nov 2026 (PR #548, bdudout): Feria's f. 143 aligned with its decipherment f. 131v gives 89 = yu, 77 = pi (pli with the loop) and len = grand- from the decipherment, ner = necesidad and gur = -mente by context only (texts/f143_alignment.md). Counted strictly (context-only values are holes) no. 68 is unchanged at 0.258 clean; the contributor's estimate with gur = -mente is about 0.266 (not measured).
texts.label: Diego de Ibarra, Paris, 10 July 1593, BnF fr. 3984 no. 68, f. 145
texts.summary: Ibarra writes from Paris during the Estates of 1593 in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher: the messenger he is despatching, cavalry awaited, 'no estamos desesperados', peril, and help that might come with the cavalry. The three-letter word codes, which carry much of the sense, have no published table and stay unread.
